text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] kv-cache prefill queue depth spiking in prod-us-west-2 - rules/kv-prefill-queue (severity: P1)

alex: seeing this on dashboards now, prefill queue depth jumped ~8x at 15:02 UTC, latency for short-gen also climbing.

mira: confirmed. traces show a bunch of streaming requests hitting continuous-batcher with small prefixes causing cache churn.

sam: is there a customer page? any 5xx or errors?

alex: not 5xx, but token latency 95p up from 60ms -> 420ms for short responses. some customers reported slow chat.

opsbot: Pager sent to @sam, @mira, @alex at 15:03 UTC.

mira: I'm taking lead. initial hypothesis: a recent batch tuning change reduced batch timeout and increased prefill attempts, causing many warmup prefill ops to flood cache and keep nodes hot -> autoscale thrash.

lucy: FYI prod alerts: hpa-scale-ups 15x in last 6m; some nodes are short-lived (10-30s).

sam: can we kill prefill attempts? Is there a runtime flag to disable continuous prefill?

mira: yes, runtime has `enable_prefill` and `prefill_max_concurrency` flags exposed via SRE firewall. I can flip `enable_prefill=false` for the farm.

alex: do it. Also, reduce batching max_wait_ms to avoid forming tiny batches? but that might increase dispatches. maybe just disable prefill first.

mira: flipping `enable_prefill=false` in staging to validate quick.

opsbot: deploy job started: infra/config-update -> runtime-flags (change enable_prefill=false) by mira.

sam: on customer impact: which customers hit? any enterprise paying customers? need to notify CS if we expect >5m.

mira: fetching origin logs for top prefixes, looks like 7 tenants are generating >60% of the prefill traffic; some internal e2e tests too.

devon: I see burst from a partner region proxy that started doing small streaming requests after a deploy at ~14:58 UTC. Might be a rollout ripple.

lucy: Can we triage whether the HPA thresholds are too aggressive because of telemetry spikes from prefill? My bet: CPU probe sees eviction pressure and ramps nodes before warmup finishes, creating shorter-lived nodes and more prefill to fill new nodes -> feedback loop.

mira: infra change done in staging looks good, applying to prod now.

incident-bot: Change applied to prod at 15:11 UTC - runtime flag `enable_prefill=false`.

alex: observing metrics... prefill queue depth dropping. good sign. token latency 95p decreasing (now 180ms).

sam: HPA activity?

lucy: scale-ups reduced. but some nodes still churning due to remaining warmup traces. HPA stabilize window is 60s; maybe extend temporarily.

mira: proposing two follow-ups: 1) temporarily increase HPA stabilization to 300s to avoid re-triggering and 2) adjust `prefill_max_concurrency` default to lower value in config for next release.

alex: +1 to stabilization change. Devon please run a controlled canary with a small traffic spike to validate.

devon: can do. scheduling 15:25 UTC small spike to see behavior.

opsbot: incident timeline note created: INC-2005 (kv-prefill-queue-spike).

sam: customer comms: CS wants a brief note. Impact window so far ~15:02-15:20 UTC with elevated latency for some chat flows. No data loss, no 5xx.

mira: I can draft comms. Also capturing root cause: recent batching change increased prefill frequency and reduced batching tolerance, which interacted poorly with HPA settings leading to auto-scale thrash and cache blowup.

alex: any need for immediate rollbacks? we already toggled prefills.

mira: not for code. We'll deploy config roll-forward: increase prefill cooldown and reduce concurrency in the runtime config. Also we'll patch HPA stabilization and add a short-term admission controller to reject micro-prefill bursts.

lucy: ops change done: HPA stabilization window set to 300s at 15:18 UTC across affected autoscaling groups.

alex: metrics now near normal baseline. Maintaining watch for next 20m.

devon: canary spike executed at 15:25 UTC, cluster handled it without additional scale events, prefill queue stayed low.

sam: excellent. please add mitigations to postmortem runbook: - guardrails on prefill defaults - HPA policies with warmup hysteresis - per-customer prefill rate-limits - alert thresholds that correlate prefill queue depth + HPA churn

mira: noted. I'll own the postmortem and runbook updates. ETA EOD.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2005 status: mitigated at 15:26 UTC.

lucy: final check: any residual customer escalations?

sam: CS reported two customers noticed brief slowdowns, both acknowledged. No SLA violations. We'll follow up in ticket INC-2005.

alex: huge thanks to everyone for fast triage. Action items: mira -> postmortem + config PR; lucy -> HPA policy PR; devon -> add canary test to deploy pipeline; sam -> CS note draft.

mira: will post the timeline and root cause later.

opsbot: Reminder: please add reactions for any blocked follow-ups. :thumbsup:

alex: :thumbsup:
